holidays.name: Islamic New Year
holidays.explanation: The first day of Muharram starts a new Hijri year. In Diyanet calendars, it is treated as a day of remembrance and self-renewal, connected to the Hijrah era. Many Muslims mark it with personal reflection, additional prayers, and intention-setting for the year ahead.

holidays.name: Ashura
holidays.explanation: Ashura is observed on 10 Muharram. In Sunni tradition, it is associated with Allah granting deliverance to Prophet Musa and his people. Diyanet guidance commonly highlights voluntary fasting on this day, gratitude, charity, and remembrance.

holidays.name: Mawlid al-Nabi
holidays.explanation: Mawlid al-Nabi commemorates the birth of Prophet Muhammad. Diyanet programs typically emphasize learning his character and mercy through recitation, sermons, salawat, and community gatherings focused on moral and spiritual renewal.

holidays.name: Regaib Night
holidays.explanation: Regaib Night (Regaib Kandili) is one of the sacred nights in the Three Holy Months season. In Turkish and Diyanet tradition, it is observed through night prayers, Quran recitation, dua, repentance, and renewal of intention before Ramadan.

holidays.name: Isra and Mi'raj Night
holidays.explanation: Isra and Mi'raj Night (Mirac Kandili) commemorates the Prophet's night journey and ascension. Diyanet-centered observance focuses on the spiritual lessons of faith, prayer, and steadfastness, with special worship and remembrance at night.

holidays.name: Bara'at Night
holidays.explanation: Bara'at Night (Berat Kandili), observed in mid-Sha'ban, is traditionally treated as a night of seeking forgiveness and mercy. Diyanet teachings often emphasize tawbah, reconciliation, and sincere dua in preparation for Ramadan.

holidays.name: Ramadan Start
holidays.explanation: The first day of Ramadan begins the month of fasting from dawn to sunset. Diyanet guidance emphasizes that Ramadan is not only abstaining from food and drink, but also strengthening character, discipline, Quran recitation, and generosity.

holidays.name: Laylat al-Qadr
holidays.explanation: Laylat al-Qadr (Kadir Gecesi) is among the final nights of Ramadan and is described in the Quran as better than a thousand months. Diyanet observance highlights deep worship, Quran recitation, repentance, and prayers for forgiveness and guidance.

holidays.name: Eid al-Fitr
holidays.explanation: Eid al-Fitr starts on 1 Shawwal and celebrates the completion of Ramadan. In Diyanet practice, the day includes Eid prayer, zakat al-fitr completion, family visits, reconciliation, and support for those in need. Community khutbah themes often stress gratitude, social solidarity, and preserving Ramadan's ethical discipline beyond the month.

holidays.name: Day of Arafah
holidays.explanation: The Day of Arafah on 9 Dhu al-Hijjah is central to Hajj and is regarded as one of the most virtuous days of the year. Diyanet resources commonly encourage fasting for non-pilgrims, abundant dua, and remembrance throughout the day. Educational materials also highlight repentance, rights of others, and preparing spiritually for Eid al-Adha.

holidays.name: Eid al-Adha
holidays.explanation: Eid al-Adha begins on 10 Dhu al-Hijjah and commemorates Prophet Ibrahim's devotion and trust in Allah. Diyanet observance centers on Eid prayer, sacrificial worship for those able, and distributing meat to relatives, neighbors, and vulnerable families. Guidance also emphasizes proper welfare and hygiene standards in sacrifice handling, and prioritizing dignity for recipients.
